part1_item1.notes:
[chunk 1/2] Filing: MSFT 10-Q for Q3 FY2024 (period ending March 31, 2024). Key extractions:

1. INFLECTION RELATED-PARTY: Microsoft obtained a non-exclusive IP license from Inflection AI in March 2024. Board member Reid Hoffman co-founded Inflection and sits on its board; entities he may beneficially own held <10% equity. Classic governance/circularity risk — board member's portfolio company becomes a Microsoft IP licensor. Severity 3.

2. CAPEX SURGE: PP&E additions of $30.6B in 9M FY2024 vs $19.2B prior-year period (+60% YoY). Depreciation, amortization & other jumped from $10.0B to $15.9B over the same period. No specific named counterparty for the bulk of capex in this filing section (OpenAI commitment details not restated here). Severity 3.

3. VIE NON-CONSOLIDATION: Microsoft explicitly states it is not the primary beneficiary of any VIE investment and does not consolidate them. Equity investments "Other" category (equity method + measurement alternative) grew from $7.2B to $10.2B — a $3B increase in 9 months, likely including the OpenAI equity stake at cost/equity method. Severity 2.

4. SERVER-COMPONENT RECEIVABLES: $10.1B in "other receivables related to activities to facilitate the purchase of server components" — an unusual balance sheet item that likely represents MSFT acting as intermediary/guarantor for supplier financing, obscuring true capex and concentration. Severity 2.

5. ACTIVISION GOODWILL OPACITY: $51B of goodwill from Activision remains "preliminary" as of this filing. Substantially all non-deductible for tax. Severity 2.

6. EQUITY IMPAIRMENTS: $199M in equity investment impairments in 9M FY2024 vs $16M prior year, plus $792M in "Other, net" losses primarily from equity-method losses — signals stress in private portfolio. Severity 2.

No SPVs or off-balance-sheet project finance structures were explicitly named in this section of the filing. The OpenAI $13B+ investment is not restated as a specific line item in this quarterly note but is embedded in the equity investments "Other" category ($10.2B measurement-alternative bucket).
[chunk 2/2] Key findings from MSFT 10-Q (filed 2024-04-25, period ending March 31, 2024):

1. HIDDEN LEVERAGE (Severity 4): $87.8B in uncommenced finance leases + $8.4B uncommenced operating leases, primarily for datacenters, not yet on balance sheet. Existing on-balance finance lease liabilities are $22.9B and operating lease liabilities are $17.9B. Combined future datacenter lease obligations exceed $116B. These leases commence FY2024–FY2030 with terms up to 20 years.

2. CAPEX ROI GAP (Severity 3): The $87.8B uncommenced finance leases represent locked-in future obligations with no specifically matched contracted revenue disclosed. Remaining performance obligations of $242B (45% recognized in next 12 months) provide partial macro-level offset but are not contract-matched to specific capacity.

3. IRS TRANSFER PRICING (Severity 3): IRS seeking $28.9B additional tax payment plus penalties and interest for tax years 2004–2013. Unrecognized tax benefits of $23.8B on balance sheet. No near-term resolution expected.

4. No named AI lab investments, OpenAI-related disclosures, or SPV/JV structures were present in this specific section of the filing. The OpenAI investment relationship would appear in other notes (e.g., Note 8 investments) not included in this excerpt.

5. Commercial paper: $20.5B outstanding at 5.4% weighted average rate — routine short-term liquidity, not extracted as SIFI-material on its own.

part1_item2.notes:
[chunk 1/2] 
SOURCE: Microsoft 10-Q, filed 2024-04-25 (Q3 FY2024, period ending March 31, 2024), Part I Item 2 MD&A.

KEY FINDINGS:

1. CAPEX ROI GAP (severity 3): Microsoft explicitly signals that capex will "increase in coming years" for AI infrastructure and training, but provides no committed revenue offset. Cloud gross margin already compressed slightly to 72%. No specific dollar commitment is quantified in this section (the Notes to Financial Statements were not included in this extract).

2. SUPPLIER CONCENTRATION – GPUs (severity 3): Microsoft discloses datacenter dependency on GPUs from "very few qualified suppliers" — a clear single-source dependency signal pointing to NVIDIA dominance, though NVIDIA is not named explicitly in this section.

3. COST OPACITY – Depreciation Life Change (severity 2): Multiple references to "change in accounting estimate for the useful lives of our server and network equipment" that flattered gross margin and operating income. The actual life-extension parameters are in the 10-K; this MD&A repeatedly strips out its effect in its "excluding" commentary, signaling it was material to headline numbers.

4. IRS TAX CONTINGENCY (severity 3): $28.9B proposed IRS adjustment for tax years 2004–2013 on intercompany transfer pricing. While Microsoft disputes it, the magnitude (>40% of quarterly revenue) is SIFI-material.

5. EQUITY METHOD LOSSES & INVESTMENT GROWTH: Equity and other investments surged from $9.9B to $14.8B (+$4.9B) in 9 months — likely driven by the OpenAI equity stake expansion — while "Other, net" shows net recognized losses on equity method investments ($486M in Q3 alone, $792M YTD). This signals the OpenAI investment may be accounted for as equity method with losses flowing through the P&L, but OpenAI is not named in this MD&A section.

6. OFF-BALANCE-SHEET DISCLOSURE: Microsoft explicitly states "We have not engaged in any related party transactions or arrangements with unconsolidated entities or other persons that are reasonably likely to materially affect liquidity or the availability of capital resources." This is a clean negative assertion — no off-balance-sheet SPVs extracted.

7. ACTIVISION BLIZZARD: $75.4B acquisition completed October 13, 2023. Not a hidden leverage signal — fully consolidated and on-balance-sheet.

LIMITATIONS: This extract covers only the MD&A narrative (Part I, Item 2). The Notes to Financial Statements (Part I, Item 1) — which would contain the OpenAI investment details, operating lease schedules, purchase obligations table, and debt note — were not provided. A complete extraction would require those notes, particularly Note 8 (investments), Note 10 (debt), and the purchase obligations footnote.

[chunk 2/2] This section (MD&A Items 3–4, Part II Items 1–1A) is primarily a market risk sensitivity table and early competitive risk factor disclosure. No off-balance-sheet entities, capex commitments, SPVs, or named AI-lab/compute-provider investments are disclosed in this excerpt. Key quantitative signals extracted: FX revenue sensitivity $9.5B (10% move), equity portfolio sensitivity $1.08B (10% move), interest rate sensitivity $1.47B (100bp move), credit sensitivity $334M (100bp move). No SIFI-material hidden leverage, circularity, revenue roundtripping, or named counterparty concentration signals appear in this text block. The filing sections covering OpenAI investment, Azure capex buildout, and off-balance-sheet obligations would appear in other sections (Notes to Financial Statements, Part I Item 1) not included here.

part2_item1a.notes:
[chunk 1/2] Filing: MSFT 10-Q 2024-04-25 (Part II Item 1A). Key SIFI-material extractions:

1. CIRCULARITY / DEPENDENCY: Microsoft explicitly names OpenAI as its "strategic partner" for AI capabilities underpinning Azure, Copilot, Bing, and other products. Microsoft is simultaneously OpenAI's largest investor, cloud infrastructure provider, and distribution channel — a classic investor⇄customer⇄supplier triangle. Severity 3 (elevated).

2. CAPEX ROI GAP: Microsoft acknowledges escalating datacenter/infrastructure costs for AI that "will reduce the operating margins we have previously achieved," without disclosing matched contracted revenue to cover the build-out. Severity 3.

3. SUPPLIER CONCENTRATION: GPU and datacenter component supply is called out as limited-supplier risk, implicitly flagging NVIDIA dependency, though NVIDIA is not named by name in this section. Severity 3.

4. HIDDEN LEVERAGE / TAX: The IRS NOPAs for $28.9B plus penalties and interest for transfer pricing (2004-2013) represent a contingent liability not fully reflected on-balance-sheet. This is material at SIFI scale. Severity 4 (critical).

5. EXECUTION RISK: The November 2023 nation-state password-spray breach of Microsoft email accounts and source code repositories is an ongoing, unresolved operational risk with cascading customer impacts. Severity 3.

6. M&A RISK: Activision Blizzard acquisition ($68.7B, completed Oct 2023) remains subject to active FTC challenge that could alter or unwind the transaction. Goodwill impairment risk also flagged. Severity 3.

No off-balance-sheet SPVs or revenue roundtripping arrangements were named in this section. No individual capex dollar commitments tied to specific counterparties were disclosed in this section (those appear in financial statements/MD&A).
[chunk 2/2] Section reviewed: Microsoft 10-Q filed 2024-04-25, Part II Item 1A (Risk Factors interim) and Item 2 (Share Repurchases). No SIFI-material entities were identified. The risk factors present are generic/boilerplate in nature: macroeconomic conditions, geopolitical risk (Ukraine conflict mentioned generically), climate change, workforce/unionization, and investment portfolio risks (U.S. government securities). No named counterparties with concentration risk, no SPVs/off-balance-sheet entities, no AI lab investments, no capex commitments, no circularity patterns, no revenue roundtripping, and no supplier/customer concentration disclosures meeting the SIFI-material threshold. Item 2 covers routine share repurchases and dividends — no related-party angle. Nothing extracted per hard rules: do not fabricate, skip boilerplate.
